                        </ns0:gap>. Mon<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tanus</ns0:hi> translateth it, <ns0:hi>from the sufficiency</ns0:hi> of my speaking with him; the reason of the difference is, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> signifies to <ns0:hi>suffice,</ns0:hi> and it sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifies <ns0:hi>time.</ns0:hi> I see no reason to vary from our Translation, <ns0:hi>since</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>from the time</ns0:hi> as the same particle signifieth, 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 18.30. 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 14.28. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 28.19. I spake against him by my threat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nings<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> I do remember him with the affection and compassion of a Father.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deu 32.36. Isa. 63.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Hos. 11.8.</ns0:note> therefore my bowels are <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>sou<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>d.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> troubled for him, I will surely have mercy upon him, saith the LORD.<ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">My <ns0:hi>bowels are troubled for him,</ns0:hi> is as much as I have pitied him; as the Bowels of Parents are turned and trou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bled for their children in Calamities; therefore saith God,</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">I will certainly shew him Favour.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:42" />21 Set thee up way-marks <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The latter part of this verse expounds the former. Thou shalt (saith God) return again to these Cities which thou now leavest, therefore take good notice of the way thou goest, set up <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ome marks by which thou mayest know it again.</ns0:note>, make thee high heaps <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Make thee Pillars or some high heaps of Stone in the way, which thou mayest know again when thou comest at them.</ns0:note>: set thine heart towards the high-way, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> the way <ns0:hi>which</ns0:hi> thou wentest <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Mind well the way that the <ns0:hi>Assyrians</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Babylonians</ns0:hi> carried thee, for thou shalt come back the same way.</ns0:note>: turn again, O virgin of Israel, turn again to these thy ci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ties <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Further to assure them they should return, he calls to them to <ns0:hi>turn again,</ns0:hi> and dou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bleth his words, for the further confirmation of the thing.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 ¶ How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">That the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> are here meant by the backsliding daughter is out of question; but what <ns0:hi>going about</ns0:hi> is here intended, is not so plain. Some interpret it of their running after Idols; some, of their seeking help from forreign Nations, instead of applying themselves unto God. Others of their wandring up and down in Captivity.</ns0:note>? for the LORD hath created a new thing in the earth, a woman shall compass a man <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">But the greater difficulty is about this <ns0:hi>new thing,</ns0:hi> which the Lord saith he will <ns0:hi>create in the new</ns0:hi> Earth, a Woman <ns0:hi>compassing a man.</ns0:hi> Some by Women understanding feeble Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons that should prevail against strong men. But the two Inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pretations of this difficult passage which seem most reasonably to contend for preference are, 1. The interpretation of those who think it contains a Promise both of the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Church in its time, and of the <ns0:hi>Gospel Church,</ns0:hi> after the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Churches period, prevailing over all its Enemies, whether Temporal or Spiritual, though considering the paucity of the Churches Members with the multitude of its Enemies and their power: it seemed as strange a thing, as for a Woman to prevail against a strong and mighty man. This the learned Author of the <ns0:hi>English Annotati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons,</ns0:hi> judgeth the true and genuine sense of these words. Others interpret this Woman to be the <ns0:hi>Virgin Mary,</ns0:hi> who was to inclose in her Womb the Lord Jesus Christ, to whom the converted <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were to adhere; which sense neither Mr. <ns0:hi>Calvin,</ns0:hi> nor our learned <ns0:hi>English Annotator</ns0:hi> approve of. But it being the receiv'd sense of very many Interpreters, it is fit we should hear their Reasons, which are 1. They urge the particle <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, for God, they say, here gives the Reason why the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> should desire to return into the country of <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> because the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> was to be born there. 2. They urge the term <ns0:hi>created,</ns0:hi> the body of Christ being not be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gotten by man, but created by God, though of the Flesh of the Virgin. 3. They say this indeed was a new thing. It was a new thing for a Virgin to become a Mother, still remaining a Vir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gin, and to be the Mother of him who was God blessed for ever, though not the Mother of the Divine Nature, for so Christ an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swered the Type of <ns0:hi>M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>lchisedeck,</ns0:hi> without <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> as Man, without <ns0:hi>Mother</ns0:hi> as God. 4. All other incompassings of a man they say were as well out of <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi> as in it, this was in <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi> only. 5. The word translated <ns0:hi>Woman</ns0:hi> in Scripture, they say alwayes signifies a particular individual Woman, which could be no other than the Virgin. 6. They say the whole context refers to benefits com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing by Christ, therefore he must certainly be the man here in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tended. 7. They urge that this Prophecy follows <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 15. which <ns0:hi>Matt.</ns0:hi> 2.8. is applyed by the Evangelist to <ns0:hi>Herods</ns0:hi> Mur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der of the Infants upon the Birth of Christ. But on the other side it is objected that the Verb <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> is never used in Scripture to signifie such an <ns0:hi>incompassing.</ns0:hi> 2. That the word translated <ns0:hi>a man,</ns0:hi> signifying a <ns0:hi>strong man,</ns0:hi> doth not properly agree to an In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fant in the Mothers Belly. But it is again replied, that this is not the onely word in Scripture, that is but once read in the same sense. 2. That the word signifieth any incompa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sing<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and may properly be applied to the Virgins Womb incompassing an Infant. And for the word translated <ns0:hi>Man,</ns0:hi> they say it is ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plied to a new born <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>nfant, <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 3.3. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 9.6. That it is ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plied to God <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 10.17. and to Christ, <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 13.7. compar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed with <ns0:hi>Math.</ns0:hi> 26.31. In a matter wherein so many Learned men are divided, it is enough for me to give their Opinions and Reasons, leaving my Reader to his own <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>udgment, in a mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter wherein neither his Faith nor Holiness are much concerned, for the Question is not concerning the thing, whether Christ was incompassed in the Womb of a Woman, which is plain e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nough from other Scriptures, but onely whether that be the sense of the phrase here.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 Thus saith the LORD of hosts the God of Israel <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">These Prophesies of the Restauration of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> are very ordinarily prefaced with these two Attributes of God, the one of which asserts his Power to do the thing promised; for what cannot be done by the Lord of Hosts? the other asserting his Goodness or good Will to this People, because he is their God, related to them, in Covenant with them, A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bility and Love or Good Will to us, being the two Pil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lars of our Faith and Confidence in God, which requireth no more than that we should be assured that the Person whom we trust is able and willing to do what we trust to him for.</ns0:note>, As yet <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">The particle <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> seemeth better translated <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 5. <ns0:hi>yet again they shall use,</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note> they shall use this speech in the land of Judah, and in the cities thereof, when I shall bring again their captivity, The LORD bless thee, O habitation of justice, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> mountain of holiness <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Three things the Prophet here foretelleth. 1. That the cities which had formerly been the Habitations of bloody, unjust, cruel men should become the Habitations of men who should do justice to all. 2. That the City which stood upon Mount <ns0:hi>Z<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>on,</ns0:hi> and had formerly been an habitation of Idolaters, and other unholy Persons should become a place, in which men should in a due and holy manner serve and worship the true God. 3. That the<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> should be so famous both for Justice and Holiness<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that men should take notice of it, and wish them well under that notion, and upon that account, as they had for their sins been made a Curse and a Proverb, so upon their Reformation they should be for a Blessing. By this we may observe that those who would be blessed by God and Men, must be just toward men, and holy towards God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 And there shall dwell in Judah it self, and in all the cities thereof together husbandmen, and they <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> go forth with flocks <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">This whole Verse is but an expression of their peaceable state after their return, they should live innocently and peace<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ably. So <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 33.12.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 For I have satiated the weary soul, and I have replenished every sorrowful soul <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">I <ns0:hi>have</ns0:hi> here is of the same significancy with I will, as ordinarily in prophetical Promises which are the words of him who calleth <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>he things that are not as if they were, and would have his people look upon the things which he hath promised to do as certain as if they were already done. The words are onely a promise to the same sense as before, that God would give his people abundance of ease and plenty, and wipe all tears from their eyes.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 Upon this I awaked, and beheld; and my sleep was sweet unto me <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Either this Revelation was made to <ns0:hi>Jeremiah</ns0:hi> in a dream, from whence he awaking, look'd about him, and he was very well pleased with his sleep at that time, because of the gracious Promises concerning <ns0:hi>Judah</ns0:hi> which the Lord had in that Dream revealed to him. Or else in a Vision, upon the sight and hearing of which he was as well pleased, as a man that had slept quiet<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly, and had had no ill and unpleasing but sweet and delightful dreams while he slept.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 ¶ Behold, the dayes come, saith the LORD, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Hos. 2.23.</ns0:note> I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and with the seed of beast <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">That is, I will exceedingly multiply them, both with men and with Cattel, they are now laid waste, their men are destroy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, or gone into other lands, their profitable Beasts are destroy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed and kill'd up, but it shall not be so alwayes. I will again plant them, and there shall be as great plenty of either, as if they were sown, the multiplying both of Men, and of Beasts in Nations is Gods blessing.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 And it shall come to pass, <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> like as I have watched over them to <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 1.10.</ns0:note> pluck up, and to break down and to throw down, and to destroy and to afflict; so will I watch over them to build and to plant, saith the LORD.<ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Nothing can produce in God a change of Counsels, Pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />poses and Decrees, for he is not as man <ns0:hi>that he should lie</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pent,</ns0:hi> he is <ns0:hi>the God that changeth not,</ns0:hi> but mens Reformation m<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>y produce in him a change of Providential dispensations. God is here set out as a Man that is vindicative, and his vindicative nature prompts him to watch all opportunities of doing hurt, to the person against whom he is set. There is no fury nor re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venge in God, but what he doth is justice; but here an angry God is set out, as taking all opportunities to punish sinners as if he had watched for them, whereas he never slumbreth nor sleepeth; But the time of their reformation, and his favour being come, God promiseth to be as diligent to do them good, which is here exprest by the metaphorical notions of planting and building them; as he was before to execute his justice up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:43" />29 In those dayes they shall say no more; The fathers have eaten a sowre grape, and the chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />drens teeth are set on edge <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">That is, we are punished for our Fathers sins, which yet God may justly do, and none questioneth the justice of man in the case, depriving children of their patrimonial Estates for their Parents Treasons, nor more then God threatneth in the second Commandment. God indeed <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 18.2. seemeth dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pleased at their use of this Proverb, but the reason is, because they so used it, as to acquit themselves, intimating they were guiltless, and suffered only for the sins of their Parents, where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />as that was false, otherwise the punishment of children for the sins of their Parents, was no more then God had threatned, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 20.5. and 34.7. <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 15.4. But faith God your cap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tivity shall, as to you, expiate your Parents guilt past, and you shall no more say so.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 But every one shall dye for his own ini<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quity, every man that eateth the sowre grape, his teeth shall be set on edge <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">But yet (saith God) you must not think that sinners shall escape my vengeance, but if men commit iniquity they shall dye, no mans teeth shall be set on edge, but his only, who hath eaten the sowre grape.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 ¶ Behold, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 32.40. Heb. 10.16.</ns0:note> the dayes come, saith the LORD, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Ju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dah <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">The Apostles application of this, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 8.8.9, 10. puts us out of doubt, that this promise referred to the Gospel-times, it was not only made with the <ns0:hi>Iewes,</ns0:hi> but all those who should be ingraffed into that <ns0:hi>olive,</ns0:hi> but it is said to be made with them, either as those two terms signifie the whole Church, with whom that Covenant was made, (they being the whole Church which God had upon the Earth at that time) or because they were the onely people that had broken the first Covenant, the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> being strangers at that time to the <ns0:hi>covenant of promise, Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.12. Covenants being usually renewed upon one parties violati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of them, or because it was at first made with the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> though it concerned also those <ns0:hi>that were afar off, even as many as the Lord should call, Acts</ns0:hi> 2.39, Neither is it called the new Covenant, because it was as to the substance new, for it was made with <ns0:hi>Abraham, Gen.</ns0:hi> 17.7. and with the <ns0:hi>Iews, Deut.</ns0:hi> 26.17, 18. And it was then confirmed by the blood of Christ, though not actually shed, yet as he was <ns0:hi>the lamb slain from the beginning of the World,</ns0:hi> whose blood was Typified by the blood of the Paschal Lamb, and of all those living Creatures killed for Sacrifice, but upon many other accounts, thus enumerated by Divines. 1. Because it was new in the notion of a Testa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, not confirmed by the actual death of Christ till Gospel times. 2. Because it was revealed and preached after a new manner, more fully and particularly, plainly and clearly. 3. Because it had no such mixture of promises of temporal blessings, as it had when first made with the <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi> 4. Nor was the Ceremonial Law any part of it, as it was to the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> who were obliged to approve themselves Gods people by a strict observance of that. 5. It was in the publication extended both <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o <ns0:hi>Jewes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> which the former was not. 6. In regard of the efficacy of the spirit attending the publication of it, in a much fuller and larger manner, with the distribu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of its gifts and graces, i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>abling souls to fulfil it. See more in the <ns0:hi>English Annotations</ns0:hi> upon this Subject.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of E<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gypt <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Not in substance differing from it, but in circumstances vastly differing, as was shewed before, and is further declared afterward. The Covenant which God made with the <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> when they came out of the Land of <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> was on Gods part the Law which he gave them, with the promises annexed to their observation of it; on their part (which made it a formal Covenant) their promise of obedience to it, of which see <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 24.7, 8. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 26.17, 18. This Covenant God saith he made with them, when they were an impotent weak people, the care of whom he took upon him, and led them as a Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rent leadeth the feeble child by his hand. None must imagine that this Covenant did not contain the promise of pardon, through the blood of the Messiah, upon their application to him, for to what purpose else was it confirmed by blood, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 24.8.</ns0:note>, which my covenant they brake <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Which Covenant they are said to have broken, not because of every disobedience to the Law of God, for so every one daily breaketh it, but by their gross and eminent sinnings, so oft repeated, and continued in without repentance, and more particularly by their <ns0:hi>Id<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>l<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>try,</ns0:hi> which is compared to <ns0:hi>whoredom,</ns0:hi> which breaketh the Covenant, and bond of Marri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />age, and causeth God to say unto a people, <ns0:hi>Lo Ammi</ns0:hi> you are not my people.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>should I have continued an husband unto them.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> although I was an husband to them, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">And this <ns0:hi>Covenant breaking</ns0:hi> is aggravated from Gods kindness to them, and care of them; who had for them the love, and declared the care of an husband, and gave them no temptation to go a whoring from him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 But this <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">That is, with those <ns0:hi>Israelites indeed</ns0:hi> who shall be without <ns0:hi>guil<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> (as Christ saith of <ns0:hi>Nathaniel, Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.47.) with those who are (as the Apostle speaks <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 2.29.) <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> inwardly, by the circumcision of the heart and spirit, spoken of, and promised by God, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 30.6.</ns0:note>, After those dayes, saith the LORD, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 11<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 20. and 3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.26, 27. 2 Cor. 3.3.</ns0:note> I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">In the times of the Go<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pel, Gods Law is not abrogated and made void, Christ him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self came not to destroy the Law, but to fulfil it; but it is written in the hearts of Gods true Israel, by the finger of the spirit, not in tables of stone only, and they become obedient to it, not from compulsion and force, but from their secret ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />probation of it, and acknowledgment of it, as <ns0:hi>holy, just</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>good,</ns0:hi> the delight they take in it, <ns0:hi>after the inward man, Rom.</ns0:hi> 7.22. but some may object, how was this a new Covenant? did not God of old write his law in the hearts of his people? did not <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and other the servants of God, (of whom we read in the Old Testament) serve God out of a principle of love, and delight in his Law? <ns0:hi>Answ.</ns0:hi> Undoubtedly <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> and others did so, and the Law of God was wrote in their hearts, but it was by vertue of this <ns0:hi>new Covenant,</ns0:hi> from the free and efficacious grace of God. Mr. <ns0:hi>Calvin</ns0:hi> I think judgeth right, that the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets design here is to express the difference betwixt the <ns0:hi>Law</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Gospel.</ns0:hi> The first sheweth duty, the latter bringeth a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />long with it the <ns0:hi>grace of Regeneration,</ns0:hi> by which the heart is changed, fitted, and inabled for, and unto duty. All under the time of the Law that came to Salvation were saved, not from the Law, or by that, but by the Gospel, and this new Covenant, but this was not evidently exhibited, neither was the regenerating grace of God so common under the time of the Law, as it hath been under the Gospel, which maketh it look like <ns0:hi>a new Covenant</ns0:hi> with men, though it was the same Co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venant which God was alwayes in with his people, for what difference is there between the terms of the Covenant as reci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted here, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 24.7. and 30.22. and as made with <ns0:hi>Abraham, Gen.</ns0:hi> 17.7. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 30.6. It is further observable, that God maketh the writing the Law in peoples hearts, his own work. There were no need of Gods putting his Law into mens inward parts, if they had such an inward power (as some talk of) of themselves to do it, and could write it there with a pen of their own making. The <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> allow God a share in this work, only give man himself the greatest share. Others indeed give God nothing but the honour of giving man a <ns0:hi>reasonable soul,</ns0:hi> furnished with such a power, and that he hath done to Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thens, as well as those within the pale of the Church, and the <ns0:hi>Preaching of the Gospel</ns0:hi>; to those within the Church, as a fur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther aid and assistance to them then Heathens have, to use their natural power well. But let any understanding person judge whether this be probably the sense of this Text, or com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prehensive of all within the <ns0:hi>Covenant</ns0:hi> which God hath made with his people, or supposing this were true, what that is which differeth, one man living under the Gospel from another, but himself, and whether by this Doctrine man be not made a God to himself<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that is the principal cause of all spiritual and eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal good, which how it comporteth with the honour and glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry of God, or with this Text, and many others of like nature, I do not understand.</ns0:note>, and will be their God, and they shall be my peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple <ns0:hi>y.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, Know the LORD <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">This must not be so interpreted as if under the gospel, there should be no more need of ministerial teaching, for Christ himself sent out his Apostles to preach; nor yet as if there should be no more need of brotherly teachings, by instru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ction or correption; the contrary is commanded, <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 3.16. It is only an expression signifying the increase of knowledge, and of the fear of the Lord, that should be after the pouring out of the Spirit, we have such expressions, 1 <ns0:hi>I<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>h.</ns0:hi> 2.27. The Learned Author of our <ns0:hi>English Annotations</ns0:hi> thinks this phrase signifies, that under the gospel there should be a greater measure of means of knowledge, and of knowledge got by that means, and of clearne<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s of understanding in persons, or ability to conceive things revealed, and a greater number of persons, that should be enlightned with the saving knowledge of God: Others say, that by <ns0:hi>k<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>owing the Lord,</ns0:hi> is to be understood the first knowledge of God; Christians should not need be taught the first Rudiments; but the Apostle speaks otherwise, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 5.12. Others by <ns0:hi>knowledge</ns0:hi> understand the <ns0:hi>fear of the Lord.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>; for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 54.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> John 6.45. 1 Cor. 2.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>. 1 Joh. 2.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the great<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />est of them, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">God saith, they should all know him, but it must not be understood of the same degree, and measure but in a degree of sufficiency for the Duties which God expected from them upon their no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion and apprehension of God.</ns0:note> for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 33.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Micah 7.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Acts 10.43.</ns0:note> I will for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />give their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">God makes the root of all this Grace to be the free pardon, and remission of their sins.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:43" />35 ¶ Thus saith the LORD, which giveth the sun <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 1.16.</ns0:note> for a light by day, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Is. 51.15.</ns0:note> sea <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The word <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> is here ill translated <ns0:hi>divide,</ns0:hi> which hath led some Interpreters to think that God here hath a respect to his dividing the Red Sea, that the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> might pass over, which seemeth not at all here to be intended. The word in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deed signifieth to <ns0:hi>divide,</ns0:hi> but it also signifieth to <ns0:hi>quiet</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>bring to rest,</ns0:hi> and is so interpreted, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 50.34. <ns0:hi>Is.</ns0:hi> 34.14. and in this very <ns0:hi>chap. ver.</ns0:hi> 2. and doubtless were better here translated, which <ns0:hi>quietteth the sea</ns0:hi> when the waves thereof roar. All the acts mentioned, are acts speaking the Divine Almighty power, of him who is the Lord of all the Regiments in the Hosts of the Creation.</ns0:note> when the waves thereof roar, the LORD of hosts <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> his Name.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Is. 54.9. chap. 33.20.</ns0:note>If those ordinances <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">There are ordinances of Worship, which are God's Laws relating to his Worship, and <ns0:hi>Ordinances of Iustice,</ns0:hi> which are Gods laws, for the executing civil Justice, and Ordinances of Nature, which are Gods establishments for the working of na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tural causes in their order; these are those here spoken of,</ns0:note> depart from before me, saith the LORD, <ns0:hi>then</ns0:hi> the seed of Israel shall also cease, from being a Nation before me for ever.<ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Which shall hold and continue to the dissolution of the world, the continuance of which God pawneth as a pledge of the continuance of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> as a Nation <ns0:hi>all the dayes</ns0:hi> (so it is in the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi>) that is many dayes, or all the dayes they shall keep close with me, or which I have appointed, if we interpret it (as in our version) <ns0:hi>for ever</ns0:hi> it must be understood not of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the flesh, but, of the Church, the true <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> of God, which shall never fail.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 Thus saith the LORD <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 33.22.</ns0:note>, If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, I will also cast off all the seed of Israel for all that they have done, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">That is, I will never cast off all the seed of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> (which promise the Apostle, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 11.1, 2. proveth to have been by God made good, notwithstanding the rejection of the great body of that people) for none but God can either measure the heavens, or pierce to the center of the Earth.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 ¶ Behold the dayes come, saith the LORD, that the city shall be built to the LORD from the tower of Hananeel, unto the gate of the cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ner <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">That is, it shall be built round, as largely as ever, we read of this Tower of <ns0:hi>Hananeel, Neh.</ns0:hi> 3.1, and 12, 39. <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 14.10. it was in the South, or rather the Eastern part of the City. We read of the <ns0:hi>Gate of the corner,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 14.13. <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 14.10. most agree that it is in the North-East part of the City.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 And the measuring line shall yet go forth, over against it, upon the hill Gareb, and shall compass about to Goah <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">That is, it shall be built round about upon its old founda<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions, <ns0:hi>vid. Neh.</ns0:hi> 3. We are ignorant of the Ancient Scituation of the City, so are the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> themselves, therefore it is vain to pretend to an exact skill in these names of places, some say, <ns0:hi>Gareb,</ns0:hi> signifies a <ns0:hi>scab,</ns0:hi> and the Hill had its name from Leprous persons lying there.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 And the whole valley of the dead bodies <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">A valley so called (as some think) from the multitude of <ns0:hi>Senacherib's</ns0:hi> Army slain there; or, (as others think) from the Bodies of Malefactors put to death at <ns0:hi>Golgotha</ns0:hi> (which was near) cast, or buried there.</ns0:note>, and of the ashes <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">So called (as is thought) from the ashes of the sacrifices carried thither.</ns0:note> and all the fields unto the brook of Kidron, unto the corner of the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Neh. 3.28.</ns0:note> horse-gate to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards the east <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Some think that the horse-gate had its name from the Kings horses led out at it. The sum is, the whole City shall be built.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> holy, unto the LORD <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">All these places shall be parts of the Holy City, and Gods Name shall be sanctified and he shall be worshipped in them all.</ns0:note>, it shall not be plucked up, nor thrown down any more for ever <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">And the City for a long time shall abide, and not be plucked up, nor thrown down, for we know after many years it was plucked up by the <ns0:hi>Romans.</ns0:hi> If we interpret the word <ns0:hi>for ever</ns0:hi> of a perpetuity. The Church of God must here be understood, against which the gates of Hell shall never prevail, as Christ hath promised.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
